Doctor Patient Relationship , Rights and.question: 1) The foundation of doctor–patient relationship is:
Doctor Patient Relationship , Rights and.exp: Trust is the foundation of the doctor–patient relationship. It supports proper communication, compliance, confidentiality and informed decision-making.

Doctor Patient Relationship , Rights and.question: 2) Treating a patient with respect and dignity is mainly a:
Doctor Patient Relationship , Rights and.exp: A doctor has a duty to treat every patient with respect and dignity. This is part of ethical medical practice.

Doctor Patient Relationship , Rights and.question: 3) Maintaining confidentiality is a:
Doctor Patient Relationship , Rights and.exp: A doctor must keep patient information confidential. This duty continues unless disclosure is legally justified.

Doctor Patient Relationship , Rights and.question: 4) Obtaining informed consent is mainly the responsibility of:
Doctor Patient Relationship , Rights and.exp: The doctor must explain the procedure, risks, benefits and alternatives before taking informed consent. It is a major professional duty.

Doctor Patient Relationship , Rights and.question: 5) Acting in the patient’s best interest is a:
Doctor Patient Relationship , Rights and.exp: The doctor should act for the patient’s welfare. This reflects beneficence in doctor–patient relationship.

Doctor Patient Relationship , Rights and.question: 6) Providing competent medical care is a:
Doctor Patient Relationship , Rights and.exp: A doctor must provide care according to professional competence. Incompetent care may lead to negligence.

Doctor Patient Relationship , Rights and.question: 7) Giving accurate history is a:
Doctor Patient Relationship , Rights and.exp: The patient should provide accurate history to help proper diagnosis and treatment. Wrong or incomplete history may affect care.

Doctor Patient Relationship , Rights and.question: 8) Following medical advice is mainly a:
Doctor Patient Relationship , Rights and.exp: A patient should follow reasonable medical advice. Failure to do so may contribute to poor outcome.

Doctor Patient Relationship , Rights and.question: 9) Cooperating with treatment is a:
Doctor Patient Relationship , Rights and.exp: Patient cooperation is necessary for proper treatment. It includes taking medicines, attending follow-up and allowing examination.

Doctor Patient Relationship , Rights and.question: 10) Paying professional fees when applicable is a:
Doctor Patient Relationship , Rights and.exp: Payment of professional fees is listed as a duty of the patient when applicable. It is linked with the doctor’s right to remuneration.

Doctor Patient Relationship , Rights and.question: 11) A doctor gets the right to practise medicine after:
Doctor Patient Relationship , Rights and.exp: The right to practise medicine is obtained after BMDC registration. Without valid registration, medical practice is not legally allowed.

Doctor Patient Relationship , Rights and.question: 12) A doctor may refuse a patient except in:
Doctor Patient Relationship , Rights and.exp: A doctor has the right to choose or refuse patients, but not in emergencies. Emergency treatment is an ethical and legal duty.

Doctor Patient Relationship , Rights and.question: 13) Professional fees of a doctor are also called:
Doctor Patient Relationship , Rights and.exp: A doctor has the right to remuneration for professional service. It means professional fees.

Doctor Patient Relationship , Rights and.question: 14) Issuing medical certificates and reports is a:
Doctor Patient Relationship , Rights and.exp: A registered doctor has the right to issue medical certificates and reports. These must be accurate and authentic.

Doctor Patient Relationship , Rights and.question: 15) Maintaining professional secrecy is a:
Doctor Patient Relationship , Rights and.exp: The doctor has the right to maintain professional secrecy. It is closely linked with patient confidentiality.

Doctor Patient Relationship , Rights and.question: 16) A doctor may withdraw from a case after:
Doctor Patient Relationship , Rights and.exp: A doctor has the right to withdraw from a case after giving reasonable notice. Sudden abandonment may be unethical.

Doctor Patient Relationship , Rights and.question: 17) Right to safe and quality healthcare belongs to:
Doctor Patient Relationship , Rights and.exp: A patient has the right to safe and quality healthcare. This includes proper medical care without avoidable harm.

Doctor Patient Relationship , Rights and.question: 18) Right to know about illness, investigations and treatment belongs to:
Doctor Patient Relationship , Rights and.exp: Patients have the right to receive information about their illness, investigations and treatment. This supports informed decision-making.

Doctor Patient Relationship , Rights and.question: 19) Participation in treatment decision is a:
Doctor Patient Relationship , Rights and.exp: The patient has the right to participate in treatment decisions. This is based on autonomy.

Doctor Patient Relationship , Rights and.question: 20) A patient’s right to refuse treatment is related to:
Doctor Patient Relationship , Rights and.exp: A competent patient can accept or refuse treatment. This right is based on autonomy.

Doctor Patient Relationship , Rights and.question: 21) Right to choose or change doctor is also called:
Doctor Patient Relationship , Rights and.exp: A patient has the right to choose or change doctor. This includes the right to seek a second opinion.

Doctor Patient Relationship , Rights and.question: 22) Euthanasia means:
Doctor Patient Relationship , Rights and.option4: Painless death in incurable painful disease
Doctor Patient Relationship , Rights and.exp: Euthanasia means causing painless death of a person suffering from hopelessly incurable and painful disease. It is also called mercy killing.

Doctor Patient Relationship , Rights and.question: 23) Active euthanasia is done by:
Doctor Patient Relationship , Rights and.exp: Active euthanasia involves a direct positive act to hasten death. Example: giving a large dose of lethal drug.

Doctor Patient Relationship , Rights and.question: 24) Passive euthanasia occurs by:
Doctor Patient Relationship , Rights and.exp: Passive euthanasia means death occurs after withholding or withdrawing life support. It is an act of omission.

Doctor Patient Relationship , Rights and.question: 25) Voluntary euthanasia means euthanasia done:
Doctor Patient Relationship , Rights and.exp: Voluntary euthanasia is performed according to the will or request of the patient. The patient expresses desire for death.

Doctor Patient Relationship , Rights and.question: 26) Involuntary euthanasia means euthanasia done:
Doctor Patient Relationship , Rights and.exp: Involuntary euthanasia is done against the will of the patient. It is ethically and legally very serious.

Doctor Patient Relationship , Rights and.question: 27) Non-voluntary euthanasia is seen when the patient:
Doctor Patient Relationship , Rights and.exp: Non-voluntary euthanasia occurs when the patient is incapable of expressing wishes. Example: comatose patient.

Doctor Patient Relationship , Rights and.question: 28) First full legal euthanasia as national law was in:
Doctor Patient Relationship , Rights and.exp: The file mentions Netherlands, 2002, as the first full legal euthanasia as national law. Oregon is related to physician-assisted suicide.

Doctor Patient Relationship , Rights and.question: 29) Cognizable offence means police can arrest:
Doctor Patient Relationship , Rights and.exp: In a cognizable offence, police can arrest without warrant. Examples include murder, rape and robbery.

Doctor Patient Relationship , Rights and.question: 30) Non-cognizable offence requires:
Doctor Patient Relationship , Rights and.exp: In non-cognizable offences, police cannot arrest without warrant. Permission or order from a magistrate is required.
